title: Hierarchical community summaries for global questions
summary: The only mechanism that answers 'what does this user actually care about' — top-k retrieval structurally cannot.
description:
Run hierarchical community detection over the entity graph, produce an LLM summary per community per level, store the summaries as first-class retrievable records with `DERIVED_FROM` edges to their members, and route synthesis-intent queries (RTRV-7) to the summary level rather than to raw retrieval. Each level is a mutually-exclusive, collectively-exhaustive cover, which is what makes divide-and-conquer summarisation sound.

Summaries are ordinary memory records: they carry trust tiers (minimum across members, per STOR-5), they decay, they are erased when their members are erased (STOR-8), and they are regenerated rather than patched after erasure (GOV-6).

Acceptance: measured on a global-question set built during GRPH-4; summaries regenerate on graph change at the cadence GRPH-4 established; regeneration runs as an EVOL-1 job; summary records are correctly cascaded by STOR-8; cost per scope per refresh is reported. Depends on GRPH-4 clearing the threshold, GRPH-2, and EVOL-1. Do not start if GRPH-4 says no.
